name: homebrew-trust-required
body: source: v0.5.0 release defect — the macOS `package-install-e2e` job (`.github/workflows/release.yml`, running `e2e/install_test.go` `TestAnonymousPackageInstall`) failed with "Refusing to load formula ... from untrusted tap". Homebrew 6.0.0 (June 2026) requires third-party taps to be explicitly trusted. Because kalide's tap is added with a custom remote (`brew tap really-knows-ai/kalide https://github.com/really-knows-ai/kalide`, not the default `homebrew/<name>` remote), Homebrew refuses the per-formula `brew trust --formula` form for it and requires the tap-level `brew trust really-knows-ai/kalide` instead. inconsistency: the spec's Homebrew install flow was tap → install; it never named the trust step, so both the documented flow and the anonymous-install e2e were unsatisfiable on Homebrew 6.0.0+ (the e2e's `brew install kalide` cannot succeed from an untrusted custom-remote tap). resolution: (1) requirements.requirement.homebrew-install now requires tap → tap-level `brew trust really-knows-ai/kalide` → install, stating the Homebrew 6.0.0+ reason and adding an AC that install before trust fails; (2) requirements.requirement.readme-install-front-loading and requirements.requirement.install-docs require the trust command in the README Homebrew block and in INSTALL.md; (3) solution.component.install-docs and solution.component.homebrew-formula bodies updated — the formula itself is unchanged, trust is applied at the tap level, not inside the formula; (4) solution.component.anonymous-install-e2e must run `brew trust really-knows-ai/kalide` before `brew install kalide`; (5) Scoop is unchanged (the trust requirement is Homebrew-only): requirements.requirement.scoop-install, solution.component.scoop-manifest and the Linux/manual-download route are untouched. `brew trust` is a local decision needing no account or token, so global.constraint.anonymous-install still holds and no token step is introduced. [with user — defect and fixed flow directed by the coordinator]
